claim: Fatwa search-call telemetry is checked against requests observed at the production adapter transport boundary, then checked again after coordinator propagation.

currentServiceResponse.note: observed through the production deployment's own same-origin fatwa proxy — GET https://ezik.app/api/fatwa-proxy for health, scholars and fatwas/search, which is the path the deployed app itself takes to the service. The three x-vercel-id values above are the response headers of those three requests in that order: two verification calls and one search call, matching the local accounting this fixture proves offline. Re-observed on 2026-09-10 because item 37B merged binbaz kind 3 (the «fatawa al-duroos» section, 5,666 records the 2026-08-08 build had excluded), moving Ibn Baz and the grand total by exactly 5,666. The search call read q=al-talaq under scholar=binbaz and returned 860 results, up from 781 before the merge.

externalEvidence.productionReason: measured on 2026-09-10 against the production deployment dpl_GC4EMbSijTzcsb2gS7TpSqYyLHrd (target=production, aliased to ezik.app, built from 56f1dbc), by summing snapshot.records over the 19 rows of its GET /api/v1/scholars response. That response body is 9046 bytes and seals under sha8 9a1eb29d. This is a live production reading taken after the kind-3 promote, not a preview and not a number copied out of a report.
externalEvidence.reason: the offline round could not reach the service and said so. It was then observed on a preview, then on production. On 2026-09-10 item 37B promoted the rebuilt Ibn Baz corpus and the contract moved with it: production reports 19 scholars / 80,435 records / 24,145 for Ibn Baz, identical to the counts this fixture authors offline, so the local accounting and the live service agree rather than one standing in for the other. The readings were re-taken, not edited to agree.
